StringWithMarkup.String: Solid fullerenes are compressible because of the weak van der Waals forces between the fullerene molecules in the lattice. Various high-pressure phases of C60 and C70 have been characterized. When compressed to 70 percent of its original size, C60 becomes more than twice as hard as diamond. Thus, it could be applied as a shock absorber for high-energy collision or for reinforcing metals or plastics. Cross-linked polymers and high-performance polymer films can be obtained by cross-linking C60 with resins. These materials are very hard and thermally extremely stable.

StringWithMarkup.String: In C60-polymer composites, fast photo induced electron transfer occurs from the polymer to the C60 molecule and photoconductivity is observed. The efficiency of organic photoconductors could be improved by addition of C60. This discovery may lead to applications in xerography, laser printers, fax machines.
